name: 돛 제작 작업대
prompt:
Cinematic progressive pencil-and-ink line animation on a solid pure bright white background, edge to edge. The very first frame is an entirely empty white field. Static locked-off camera, one continuous 8-second take.

The subjects: one sailmaker dividing clean canvas into measured sections while removing a water-spoiled corner, folded replacement cloth pinned beside a seam ready to sew, a ruined adhesive patch contrasted with a firmly bonded sample, a shears blade cropped by the foreground, and an enormous finished sail suspended above the small cutting table.

0-3.5s: delicate light-graphite pencil strokes are traced visibly from endpoint to endpoint — soft, feather-light, barely pressed, like an artist's first gentle sketch, each line drawn once. No dense cross-hatching, no engraving-style shading; only airy contour lines. The large landscape forms are drawn first with rich observational detail, the main subject last, in a few precise strokes. The composition is asymmetric — the main subject sits off-center. Built progressively, never fading in.

3.5-5.5s: pale watercolor tints rise FROM INSIDE the pencil lines, within the lines — a restrained palette of creamy ecru on the canvas, navy on the seam guides, warm copper on the shears and pins, and muted coral on the rejected patch, each heavily diluted with water. The larger the area, the lighter and more watery its wash — broad fields, hills and skies receive only the palest, water-flooded tint, far lighter than the small subjects. Color blooms ONLY onto the drawn subjects — all surrounding space stays pure untouched white. The delicate pencil drawing remains the protagonist; color is only a light stain resting on the lines. Generous areas of the paper stay untouched white, and the painting dissolves into untouched white paper well before the frame — soft, wet watercolor boundaries, with generous white margins breathing on at least three sides of the image. One consistent light direction with soft believable shadows. The white background stays pure white. The sky, when present, stays essentially untouched white paper — only the palest breath of tint near the horizon and a few light pencil cloud outlines, never a fully painted sky.
5.5-8s: the needle completes the directed seam and the folded panel opens into its full triangular shape; the finished sail catches a gentle draft and pulls every new joint tight. Everything else stays perfectly still.

Style: delicate pencil-and-ink drawing with airy line weight and rich observational detail, fresh luminous watercolor, clear summer daylight, cinematic depth of foreground, middle ground and far horizon — the feel of a beautiful illustrated atlas for curious teenagers, never a kindergarten picture book. Museum-quality contemporary illustration.

Never: text, letters, numbers, hashtags, watermarks, a visible drawing hand, pen, pencil or brush in frame, primary crayon colors, muted grey or slate mood, sepia, ink-wash painting mood, fog, smiling sun, V-shaped birds, rainbows, dense cross-hatching, engraving-style shading, heavy dark outlines, dead-center composition, paint splatter, color outside the lines, paper texture, visible paper grain, window light streaks, ambient room shadows, vignette, camera movement, cuts, dissolve.
